text: Risk management is the process of dealing with possible problems before they happen. First, you need to identify risks, which means finding things that could go wrong. For example, a company might worry about losing money or having technical failures. After that, you develop mitigation strategies to reduce the impact of these risks. You may also create contingency plans, which are backup plans for emergencies. Finally, monitoring is important because risks can change over time. By checking your situation regularly, you can update your plans and stay prepared. Good risk management helps people and businesses avoid serious trouble and reach their goals more safely.
